data_notice: Public-sourced claim taken from an already-published URL. Probability is omitted where the original source did not state one word for word; those rows are verdict-only and are not in the Brier set. Link fields marked [U] are unknown and were not invented; those rows are reading-list items and are not scored.
exact_quote: We also predict a 35-65% chance that Top-Expert-Dominating AI (TED-AI), AIs that can automate all white-collar work, will arrive before 2028.
question: Will Top-Expert-Dominating AI (TED-AI) — AIs that can automate all white-collar work, as AI Futures Project defined it on 10 Nov 2026 — arrive before 2028?
population: White-collar (knowledge, office, professional) work that humans perform
denominator: All such white-collar work ('all' in the frozen quote, not a subset)
resolution_rule: Binary event ('arrive before 2028' = on or before 31 Dec 2027). KEPT if, on or before 31 Dec 2027, AI Futures Project publicly states that TED-AI as defined on 10 Nov 2026 has arrived, OR a public, checkable demonstration shows AIs can automate all white-collar work in that sense. BROKEN if the deadline passes without such a statement or demonstration. 'All white-collar work' is a high bar: remaining substantial white-collar occupations that cannot be automated is BROKEN, not a near-miss unresolvable. If AFP later publishes a more precise operational definition, use it only if it is a clarification of the 10 Nov wording, not a rewrite that narrows 'all.' The stated 35–65% is a range, not a single 0–1 probability, so probability is omitted and this row is not in the Brier set; the range is recorded in basis. UNRESOLVABLE only if AFP and the public record are gone or the frozen definition cannot be applied at all.
resolution_source: AI Futures Project published updates; occupational evidence (BLS or equivalent) only as supporting context, not as a substitute for the frozen 'all white-collar work' definition.
probability_note: No numerical probability was stated word for word by the original source; the claim is not in the Brier set.
basis: Q3.5 Timelines Update, 10 Nov 2026. The group stated a 35–65% chance; because that is a range and not a single 0–1 probability, the probability field is omitted and the claim is verdict-only, not in the Brier set.
base_rate_or_reference_class: The group's earlier 2025–2026 timeline updates and the METR report the page names as the single biggest source of evidence.
key_assumptions: The 10 Nov 2026 TED-AI definition ('AIs that can automate all white-collar work') is the resolution definition.
AFP will publish a resolution or a public demonstration will exist to apply the rule.
update_triggers: An AFP update that moves the TED-AI probability or arrival window.
A public claim that all white-collar work is automatable.
Clear contrary evidence that major white-collar occupations remain non-automatable near the deadline.
